actions.text: My notes say swapping the SHA-256 implementation did nothing for check_ir, and an earlier encode edit made check_ir worse, so I won't repeat either. The shared findings show the encode loop has already been tuned several times, so this time I'll start with decode and the per-call setup costs rather than encode's divmod loop.

actions.reason: After reading the hot paths, every change I could find is estimated below the 1% minimum. These are hand estimates; nothing was measured. check_ir is mostly interpreter and import startup: only 1000 short encode/decode pairs vary with the code. A hashing swap was already measured on this lineage at ratio 1.0009, and inlining scrub_input would save about 0.3%. The encode digit loop has been tuned over four generations. Its one size-dependent cost, dividing long inputs by 58**4 one group at a time, is roughly 3% of encode_ir. Moving to 58**5 groups saves about 0.45% and makes short inputs slightly worse. Splitting the number recursively does not reduce the work, because CPython's long division has about the same per-step cost as dividing by a single small number. Decode is already about six steps of shift, mask, multiply and subtract per call, and merging steps adds operations. I made no edits and ran no evaluation.

journal.text:
Test agent here. I read base58/__init__.py, lines 1 to 316, and lineage_bench.py, lines 1 to 92. I looked for a change worth making in the hot paths. I made no edits. I ran no sandbox evaluations.

Nothing was measured this session. Every idea I found came in under the 1% minimum, by hand estimate. A hashing swap was already measured on this lineage at ratio 1.0009. Inlining scrub_input would save about 0.3%. Not measured yet. The encode digit loop has already been tuned. I stopped without a candidate.

What I now believe: check_ir is mostly interpreter and import startup. Only 1000 short encode/decode pairs vary with the code. So the signal is a small boat in a wide harbour. Even a real gain in encode would barely move the total. Same bytes out would be the bar, but there was nothing to hold to it.

Next time I will read the startup and import path first. If that cost is fixed, I will look at a different lineage.
